schoolDay.context: Project default school day. It is configurable at the school profile layer; it is not a jurisdictional requirement.

occupants.uncertainty: A fictional classroom occupancy used only when the caller does not supply a profile.

roomVolumeM3.uncertainty: A fictional classroom volume used only when the caller does not supply a profile.

initialPm25.uncertainty: An initialization convention, not an indoor observation. The caller may supply an explicit initial indoor concentration.

initialCo2.uncertainty: A global-average proxy, not a local outdoor measurement. The caller may supply an explicit initial indoor concentration.

closedAirChangesPerHour.context: Winter, C130 mechanically ventilated classroom with windows reported closed at Estover Community College, Plymouth, UK; not a measurement of a ClearClass school.

source.issuer: Innovate UK Building Performance Evaluation; AECOM, University of Exeter and University of Bath
source.title: Estover Community College Campus, Appendix 10.9.1

closedAirChangesPerHour.uncertainty: Case-study rate cannot represent another room or climate. A real school must provide room-specific assessed airflow.

openAirChangesPerHour.context: Lower end of the 5 to 20 air changes per hour measured in winter with windows open in the same C130 classroom; comparative demo only.

source.issuer: Innovate UK Building Performance Evaluation; AECOM, University of Exeter and University of Bath
source.title: Estover Community College Campus, Appendix 10.9.1

openAirChangesPerHour.uncertainty: The source range reflects one classroom in specific weather/building conditions. This lower-bound illustration does not predict local window performance.

penetrationFactor.context: EPA IECCU tutorial assumes 0.8 for 2.5-µm particles in a residential PM example; not a classroom penetration measurement.
penetrationFactor.uncertainty: Penetration depends on particle size, building envelope and window state; 0.8 is an illustrative model input only.

depositionPerHour.context: Representative PM2.5 deposition rate in a residential exposure-factor table; used here only as an uncertain model parameter, not a classroom measurement.

source.title: Exposure Factors Handbook, Chapter 19: Building Characteristics

depositionPerHour.uncertainty: Deposition depends on particle size, surface, air movement, and room characteristics.

generationLitresPerMinutePerPerson.context: ASHRAE's example for sedentary people at 1.2 met. Age, body mass, and activity change generation; it is not a child-specific measurement.

source.title: ANSI/ASHRAE Addendum d to Standard 62.1-2016
source.page: p. 3, Informative Appendix D (example: 1.2 met sedentary persons, 0.31 L/min CO2 generation)

generationLitresPerMinutePerPerson.uncertainty: The addendum deletes this informative appendix and its calculation assumes sedentary 1.2-met people. Actual occupants' age, body mass, and activity must be supplied for a room-specific calculation.

outdoorPpm.context: Global annual outdoor concentration reported for 2024; local outdoor CO2 can differ materially by place and time.

source.issuer: ASHRAE citing NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory
source.title: Position Document on Indoor Carbon Dioxide
source.page: p. 8 (426 ppmv in 2024; daily, seasonal, urban, and local variation)

outdoorPpm.uncertainty: A global value is a model boundary condition, not a local measurement.

goodVentilationIndicatorPpm.context: England DfE operational guidance says under 800 ppm indicates good ventilation; it is not a global legal limit or direct health threshold.

source.title: Ventilation and air quality in education and childcare settings
source.page: Knowing what to do with your CO2 readings

concernPpm.context: England DfE operational guidance says over 1500 ppm indicates poor ventilation and to increase ventilation where possible. It is used as a model feasibility indicator only, not a universal compliance or health threshold.

source.title: Ventilation and air quality in education and childcare settings
source.page: Knowing what to do with your CO2 readings

openingPolicy.context: A bounded search of a closed schedule and six hourly 10-minute flush schedules. An applicable local school policy may set allowOpening false; this model does not infer that opening is safe in a particular room or outdoor-air episode.

source.title: Ventilation and air quality in education and childcare settings
source.page: Making sure there is enough ventilation (example: open windows and doors for 10 minutes an hour during lesson breaks)

openingPolicy.uncertainty: DfE guidance applies to England. The schedule is a project search bound, not a rule for every school or a substitute for local safety, fire, temperature, accessibility, or air-quality decisions.

methodSources.title: Indoor Air Quality Model for Particulate Matter
methodSources.page: 2001, pp. 1–18 (indoor PM mass balance includes outdoor concentration, air-exchange rate, penetration, deposition, and indoor sources)

methodSources.title: Ventilation FAQs Frequently Asked Questions
methodSources.page: FAQ 3 (CO2 can indicate ventilation but does not directly predict infection risk); FAQ 7 (ACH definition and imperfect-mixing caveat)

methodSources.title: Ventilation in Schools and Childcare Programs
methodSources.page: Bring in outdoor air (open windows and doors only when safe); Check HVAC settings

limitations: Estimated from a single-zone, well-mixed model; not measured.
CO2 is a ventilation indicator, not a complete IAQ, infection-risk, or health-safety measure.
The optional reference-case airflow rates are from one 2014 UK classroom, not measured at the selected school or transferable as a safety guarantee.
The model excludes indoor PM sources, filtration, outdoor CO2 variation, interzonal flow, weather, and room-specific airflow measurements.
Reference guidance is not a local legal requirement or a claim of compliance.
